technocore.head_message:
perf(http): compress responses with brotli, gzip fallback (#860)

## What

Responses are now compressed on the wire. Callers see no change in bytes
— compression is a transport encoding, so a client decodes to exactly
what it got before, and the export stays byte-exact for offline
re-verification.

## Why

#859: the CDN asks this origin for `gzip, br` on every request (16,782
of 16,782 in one capture) and the service answered every one in
plaintext, so the whole metered origin leg was uncompressed.

Brotli rather than Starlette's built-in `GZipMiddleware` because on this
service's own payloads it wins on **both** axes, which seemed the only
honest reason to take a dependency: streamed in `store.EXPORT_CHUNK`
blocks, br q=4 is 2.62x at 162 MB/s against gzip-6's 2.35x at 66 MB/s.
`bench/compression.py` reproduces it. The cost is stated in
`pyproject.toml`: this is the first dependency that brings its own, and
dropping to `GZipMiddleware(compresslevel=4)` is a three-line swap
keeping ~88% of the win — happy to take that instead.

`application/x-ndjson` is not in the library's default allow-list, so
`/r/<room>/export` — the largest lane by far — needs the explicit
`add_compress_type`. `tests/http/test_compression.py` covers that
specific silent failure.

One existing assertion in `test_docs.py` moved: `Vary` is now `Accept,
Accept-Encoding` on the negotiating documents, so it checks the `Accept`
dimension rather than the whole header.

## Note for merge

This grows `core/app.py` 1020 -> 1023 code lines. It is inside the
policy cap (1030, so `sz.py --caps` and the PR's CI are green), but it
moves the ratchet, so main will want `uv run sz.py --update-baseline`
after merge — the deliberate step the workflow comment describes for
growth. The three lines are an import, `add_compress_type` and the
middleware entry; `CompressMiddleware` takes no content-type argument,
so none of them consolidates away.

## Checks

- [x] `uv run coverage run -m pytest tests -q && uv run coverage report`
— 775 passed, 1 skipped, 97.97%
- [x] `uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .` and `uv run
ty check`
- [x] Docs that would now be wrong are updated: none — no served
document states an encoding
- [x] New surface on a world-writable service: **nothing new.** No new
route or parameter. Compression can leak a secret only where one is
stable across responses that mix in attacker-controlled bytes (BREACH);
there is no auth, no cookie and no session here, and the one
per-response secret — the `/humans` CSP nonce — is regenerated every
response.
